findings.title: Keep the geometrical-regime qualifier attached to the depth-of-field conclusion
findings.before:
This conclusion applies where geometrical defocus dominates;
at very small apertures, diffraction also blurs the image.
findings.after:
Sufficient sharpness need not make every defocus circle a mathematical point.
This holds where geometrical defocus dominates.
findings.precedingRepairedClaim: Stopping down makes a range of object distances look sufficiently sharp: depth of field increases.
findings.observation: The original domain restriction explicitly qualified the preceding stopping-down/depth-of-field conclusion. In the repair, This holds immediately follows the mathematical-point disclaimer in a separate paragraph, so its nearest antecedent is that disclaimer. The depth-of-field claim is also rewritten from can therefore make to makes. The later diffraction sentence remains present, but does not disambiguate what This holds qualifies.
findings.impact: The changed paragraph is grammatically complete and numerically compliant, but does not unambiguously preserve the scope of the earlier qualified claim for a learner reading paragraph by paragraph.
findings.criterion: Affected paragraph coherence and semantic preservation against the before text
findings.requiredCorrection: Name the stopping-down/depth-of-field conclusion explicitly in the geometrical-defocus qualifier, or keep that qualifier with the conclusion, while retaining the diffraction caveat and two-to-three complete sentences per paragraph.
findings.scopeQualification: This is a textual before/after attachment finding, not a repeated SCI review or a new scientific/visual verdict.
